node.statement: C*-square bootstrap. Let a_n and b_n be the lower modulus and norm of gamma_n. Exact involution preservation, the K_hom e multiplicative defect from node 1.2, the exact C*-identity in the source, and the epsilon-C* inequalities in the target give, for a universal D, b_n^2 <= (b_n+D e)/(1-epsilon) and a_n^2 >= (a_n-D e)/(1+epsilon). The preliminary bounds c_0<=a_n<=b_n<=5 select the large root of the second quadratic when e is below a universal threshold; solving the two scalar quadratic inequalities yields b_n<=1+K_boot e and a_n>=1-K_boot e, with K_boot universal and independent of n. This is the asserted two-sided complete norm estimate.
